providers.acl_description: Captures list-level access: a private list's entries are visible to its admins and the members it is shared with (resolved to member emails); team grants are not exposed by Attio's API, so team-only readers are not included. Records, notes, tasks and meetings are workspace-visible.
Captures channel-level access: public channels are visible to the whole workspace, private channels only to their members (resolved to member emails).

Captures team-level access: a public team is readable by every caller in the tenant, a private team only by its members (resolved to member emails). Documents are governed by their owning team. Project resources make no claim and are not governed.
Captures repo visibility; private repos additionally capture the collaborator list when every collaborator has a visible public email, otherwise a customer rule governs.
Captures per-file sharing (user, group, domain, and public grants) and detects permission-only changes between syncs via the Drive changes feed.
Captures the provider's own access permissions as document ACLs, enforced when a search request carries an acl list.
Captures who holds Browse access per project and per-issue security levels.
Captures space-level view permissions (groups expanded to member emails) and per-page view restrictions.

Captures per-file sharing from the containing shared folder, resolved to member emails, including Dropbox team groups when the team scopes are granted. A folder whose group cannot be expanded is left unrestricted rather than hidden.

Captures per-ticket access from the group the ticket is assigned to, resolved to agent emails, plus its assignee, its requester and every admin. Comments and satisfaction ratings inherit their ticket's audience; an internal note additionally excludes the requester.
Captures the provider's own access permissions as document ACLs, enforced when a search request carries an acl list.
Captures the provider's own access permissions as document ACLs, enforced when a search request carries an acl list.

Captures who can read each service, schedule and escalation policy from PagerDuty's base roles: owners and admins see everything, everyone else sees a team-owned object only from inside one of its teams. Incidents follow their service.

Captures access rules where they can be read. A knowledge base comes from its user criteria, and is closed rather than opened when it specifies no Can Read list and the instance sets glide.knowman.block_access_with_no_user_criteria. A ticket or custom table comes from the roles on its read rules, resolved to member emails including a role held through a group. Catalog ITEMS carry their own audience per item, since a catalog has none of its own. Knowledge ARTICLES carry theirs too, but only on an instance that enables glide.knowman.apply_article_read_criteria, which is off by default and while off means ServiceNow ignores an article's Can Read list entirely; an article that does claim one is intersected with its knowledge base, because ServiceNow requires passing both. A rule carrying a condition or a script, and a script-based user criterion, have no audience that can be read from outside the instance, so that resource or record makes no claim and stays unrestricted with a warning. Most instances carry a scripted read rule on their ticket tables out of the box.

Captures project visibility (public and internal projects are visible to everyone); private projects additionally capture every active member when each has a visible email, otherwise a customer rule governs.
Captures the provider's own access permissions as document ACLs, enforced when a search request carries an acl list.

Captures per-message access from Teams membership: a standard channel's messages are visible to the team's members, a private or shared channel's only to that channel's own members (including the members of every team a shared channel is shared with), and a chat message only to that chat's participants, all resolved to member emails. A roster that cannot be read in full leaves those messages unrestricted with a warning rather than stamping a partial allow-list.

Captures per-email access from the mailbox it was synced from: an email is visible to that mailbox's owner and nobody else. Recipients are indexed as searchable fields but are not granted access, because each recipient has their own copy in their own mailbox carrying its own audience; a recipient whose mailbox is not selected therefore does not see it at all. A mailbox whose address cannot be resolved leaves its mail unrestricted with a warning.

Captures project-level view access by evaluating each member's base role, custom roles, team roles and permission grants. Flags, segments, environments and each audit entry about one project follow that project. Members, teams and account-level audit entries are not restricted.
Captures the provider's own access permissions as document ACLs, enforced when a search request carries an acl list.
